commands.name: write-test-cases
commands.description: Plans how to test a user story before it is built, and writes the result as test cases in a document for review. Use whenever someone is getting ready to test a story, ticket or set of acceptance criteria, however they put it: test cases, test ideas, scenarios, edge cases, risks, what to check, a checklist, test design or coverage, even if they never say "test cases". Not for automated tests, test code or test data. (project)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Sync a React design system to Claude Design. Bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design."

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus broken CLAUDE.md rules and cleanups where the model's recipe covers them; see /simplify) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

commands.name: doctor

# NightJar

NightJar is a sleep diary with a gentle bedtime nudge and an AI sleep coach.
It is the running example in the course
[**Who Tests the Tests? Quality Engineering in the AI-Native SDLC**](https://softwaretestingtrends.com/courses/5d5b9470-037f-4eb4-9035-d60347980d2c).
Each lesson's recorded runs, scripts and outputs are in [`course-material/`](course-material/).

The company and team around NightJar are fictional. The app is real: it runs on
your laptop with no hardware, no phone and (by default) no API key.

> NightJar is a wellness demo, not a medical product. It never diagnoses anything.

## What it does

- **Sleep diary**: log nights (bedtime, wake time, time zone, journal notes) or import a CSV.
- **Sleep window**: your usual bedtime is the median local bedtime of your last 14 nights.
- **Wind-down nudge** (story S-114): 45 minutes before your usual bedtime, in your
  current local time, silent during quiet hours.
- **Claims register**: every phrase shown to users is checked against approved
  wellness phrases and banned disease claims (`claims/register.yaml`).
- **AI sleep coach**: answers questions from your diary. Runs on a deterministic mock
  offline, or on Claude when you add an API key. Every call is traced to `traces/coach.jsonl`.

## Setup

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). It installs Python 3.12 for you.

```bash
make install        # uv sync + Chromium for the browser test
make run            # http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

Then click **Import CSV** and choose `data/sample_nights.csv`: 21 nights for a user
in Toronto, including the March daylight-saving change and a 3-night trip to London.
The nudge panel should show **Your next wind-down nudge: 22:15**.

## Offline (mock) mode

With no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, the coach uses `MockCoach`: canned, deterministic
answers. Force it any time with `NIGHTJAR_COACH=mock`.

# One command per job. Every target exits non-zero on failure.
.PHONY: install test e2e lint format evals run

# Evals use the offline mock unless you pass NIGHTJAR_COACH=claude.
NIGHTJAR_COACH ?= mock

install:  ## install dependencies and the Chromium browser for e2e tests
	uv sync
	uv run playwright install chromium

test:  ## unit + API tests
	uv run pytest -m "not e2e"

e2e:  ## browser test (needs: uv run playwright install chromium)
	uv run pytest -m e2e

lint:  ## style and correctness checks (no changes made)
	uv run ruff check .
	uv run ruff format --check .

format:  ## auto-fix formatting
	uv run ruff check --fix .
	uv run ruff format .

evals:  ## coach evals, 3 runs per case
	NIGHTJAR_COACH=$(NIGHTJAR_COACH) uv run python evals/run_evals.py --runs 3

run:  ## start the app at http://127.0.0.1:8000
	uv run uvicorn nightjar.web:create_app --factory --reload --port 8000

__init__.py
claims.py
coach
diary.py
models.py
nudge.py
sleep_window.py
static
templates
web.py

tests:
builders.py
conftest.py
e2e
test_api.py
test_claims.py
test_coach.py
test_diary.py
test_nudge.py
test_sleep_window.py
answers. Force it any time with `NIGHTJAR_COACH=mock`.

## With Claude

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
export NIGHTJAR_COACH=claude                     # optional; a key alone selects Claude
export NIGHTJAR_COACH_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5    # optional; this is the default
make run
NIGHTJAR_COACH=claude make evals                 # real model calls cost money
```

## Checks

```bash
make test    # unit + API tests
make lint    # ruff
make e2e     # Playwright: add a night in a real browser, see the nudge
make evals   # coach evals (mock by default)
```

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `src/nightjar/` | the app (`sleep_window.py`, `nudge.py`, `claims.py`, `coach/`, `web.py`) |
| `tests/` | pytest; test names carry trace ids like `T_114_2` |
| `evals/` | coach eval cases (`cases/*.yaml`) and `run_evals.py` |
| `docs/` | requirements, story S-114, claims policy, traceability |
| `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` | instructions for coding agents |

Environment variables: `NIGHTJAR_DB` (default `nightjar.db`), `NIGHTJAR_COACH`
(`mock` or `claude`), `NIGHTJAR_COACH_MODEL`, `NIGHTJAR_TRACE_PATH`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

MIT licensed.

"""End-to-end: a real browser adds the 7th night and the nudge appears.

Needs Chromium:  uv run playwright install chromium   (skipped if it's missing)
"""

import socket
import threading
import time
from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pytest
import uvicorn
from builders import nights_at

from nightjar.coach import MockCoach
from nightjar.diary import Diary
from nightjar.web import create_app

pytestmark = pytest.mark.e2e
playwright_api = pytest.importorskip("playwright.sync_api")
NOON_IN_TORONTO = datetime(2026, 3, 20, 12, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/Toronto"))


@pytest.fixture
def base_url(tmp_path):
    diary = Diary(tmp_path / "e2e.db")
    diary.add_nights(nights_at("23:00", 6, first_night="2026-03-10"))  # one short of a nudge
    app = create_app(
        diary=diary,
        coach=MockCoach(),
        clock=lambda: NOON_IN_TORONTO,
        trace_path=tmp_path / "coach.jsonl",
    )
    with socket.socket() as sock:
        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = sock.getsockname()[1]
    server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(app, port=port, log_level="warning"))
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    while not server.started:
        time.sleep(0.05)
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    server.should_exit = True
    thread.join(timeout=5)


@pytest.fixture
def page():
    with playwright_api.sync_playwright() as playwright:
        try:
            browser = playwright.chromium.launch()
        except playwright_api.Error as error:
            pytest.skip(f"Chromium not installed ({error.message.splitlines()[0]})")
        yield browser.new_page()
        browser.close()


def test_T_114_1_e2e_adding_the_seventh_night_shows_the_nudge(page, base_url):
    page.goto(base_url)
    expect = playwright_api.expect
    expect(page.get_by_test_id("nudge-cold-start")).to_contain_text("Log 1 more night")

    page.get_by_test_id("bedtime-input").fill("2026-03-16T23:00")
    page.get_by_test_id("wake-input").fill("2026-03-17T07:00")
    page.get_by_test_id("notes-input").fill("Read a book, lights out at 11.")
    page.get_by_test_id("add-night-submit").click()

    expect(page.get_by_test_id("diary-row")).to_have_count(7)
    expect(page.get_by_test_id("nudge-time")).to_have_text("22:15")
